method: Read-only Mono.Cecil metadata over the local BepInEx interop assemblies; no assembly is loaded, no game process is started.
RVA uniqueness is the count of dump.cs method entries declaring that exact RVA; every rva below was checked to be exactly 1 unless rvaSharing says otherwise.

Direct call edges are decoded from method bodies with Iced x64; a caller body is bounded by the next dump.cs RVA and never exceeds 0x4000 bytes, so an edge listed here is a literal rel32 call at that site.
Indirect (vtable/register) dispatch is NOT decoded, so a method with no listed callers may still run through a delegate or a virtual override.

paths.identity: The deployed marker is per backpack slot, so it identifies an existing equipment life rather than a new one: the slot still holds the same BackpackItem, and the hook re-reads that slot through the already verified PlayerBackpack.Slots item pointer.
paths.owner: The backpack belongs to one player; the owner still comes from the verified SDK ResolveEntityInstance("gtfo.player") lookup, not from this hook.

Record() already refuses to publish equipped/unequipped facts for a non-Inventory location, so a deploy or a recall produces an observation change and a log line, never a fabricated wield fact.

paths.identity: A world item is a different life from a backpack item, and its resource definition is not recoverable: the payload carries pItemData/pItemData_Custom, whose itemID_gearCRC field is documented by the game as "itemID or gearCRC" and has no discriminator, and no world item table binds it to a gear definition. A recorded resource id would therefore be a guess.

paths.reason: Hooking it would create an observation with a guessed resource definition; the equipment observation contract requires a resource reference that the world payload cannot supply.

probes.note: Type names were checked for existence before anything was claimed; the task's examples resolve to real types, and names that do not exist were not used.
found: Gear.ResourcePackPickup, ConsumablePickup_Core, CarryItemPickup_Core, CommodityPickup_Core, ArtifactPickup_Core, KeyItemPickup_Core, GenericSmallPickupItem_Core (all base LevelGeneration.ItemInLevel)

limits: No claim about runtime behaviour: nothing here was executed, and a direct call edge only proves that a call site exists in the shipped binary.

Whether the game keeps a deployed slot's BackpackItem instance alive is not verified; if the instance is destroyed, the existing Matches/IsNativeCurrent logic retires the life instead of reporting a false deployed location.

SentryGunInstance.OnDespawn and SyncedPickup do not both revisit SetDeployed, so the native marker can stay set after the world instance is gone; the readback mirrors the native marker rather than repairing it.
The itemID_gearCRC field is documented by the game as carrying either an item id or a gear CRC; the backpack path resolves it through the slot's BackpackItem, the world paths have no such resolution.
